_comment: Bitwarden secrets that a workflow may hold for ONE step only. check:ci-bws-step-scope
(.ci/scripts/quality/check_bws_step_scope.py) refuses, for every name below, in every job:
(i)   a bws-secrets fetch of the name that also fetches a name not in this file;
(ii)  a step between that fetch and the last consumer that does not itself read the name;
(iii) no ./.github/actions/bws-scrub naming the exported variable immediately after the
(v)   a read of the exported variable after the scrub, or outside any fetch window.
A name is listed by its Bitwarden NAME (the left-hand side of `NAME > ENV_NAME`); the gate
derives the exported variable from each fetch line. Every name must be in
bws-secret-map.json and requested by at least one fetch, or the entry is refused as dead.
THIS LIST ONLY GROWS. The rest of the class (GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, DOCKERHUB_TOKEN, the
Cloudflare and Stripe keys) is tracked as the follow-up of

ACCOUNT_ED25519_PRIVATE_KEY.reason: BLOCKER: the production licence-signing key; any step that can read it can mint a licence every released renet accepts, and its only consumers are the per-run account server start and the Worker secret push, one step per job

ACCOUNT_X25519_PRIVATE_KEY.reason: BLOCKER: the production X25519 key the account Worker decrypts with; it is pushed to the Worker by exactly one step in each of the three deploy jobs and no other step of those jobs has any use for it

RELEASE_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY.reason: BLOCKER: the release signing key behind every Linux package and package repository; a step that reads it can publish a signed package that apt and dnf trust, and only the two cd-stage packaging steps sign anything

RELEASE_GPG_PASSPHRASE.reason: BLOCKER: the passphrase that unlocks RELEASE_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY; holding it beside the key is holding the signing capability itself, so it is scoped to exactly the same two cd-stage packaging steps
